modelingNotes: From OSM (24 mapped parts): the two 110 m side blocks (18.7 m thick, 112 m long, outer faces 106.9 m apart, tapering with 45 degree plan chamfers toward both ends of the passage), the 69.4 m wide void, and the 13 stepped parvis levels (0.63 m risers, 8.3 m platform). The frame is built along the axis joining the two side-block centroids.

Published (Wikipedia FR/EN, Paris La Defense): 112 m deep, 106.9 m wide, ~110 m high, a hollowed cube big enough for Notre-Dame, marble and glass cladding, 4 x 4 concrete transfer beams under the roof, Carrara marble on the end and void faces, glass curtain walls on the long outer faces.

Inferred: the OSM roof layers (min_height 101-108 m) are read as a 45 degree splay of the beam soffit toward the chamfered ends, and the beam soffit is set at 91.3 m so the roof beam is as deep as the side walls (18.7 m, square frame section) as the Commons photographs show. Storey pitch 2.75 m (about 39 levels). Panoramic lift core and the Nuage sail (suspended in the void, 28-40 m up) are simplified; their dimensions are not surveyed.
Materials: stone = marble, roof = grey glass curtain wall and terrace, window = glazing, trim = reveals and mullions.
